title: Lecture 7. Software Architecture: Structuring Large-Scale Programs
summary: This lecture explores fundamental techniques for organizing and structuring large software systems. Students will learn architectural thinking principles, examine common architectural styles including layered and component-based architectures, understand module dependencies and coupling, explore package organization strategies, and discover techniques for managing complexity in large-scale systems. The lecture emphasizes practical application of architectural principles to real-world software construction challenges.
learningObjectives: Understand the principles of architectural thinking and how it differs from detailed design
Apply layered architecture patterns to organize large-scale systems effectively
Design component-based systems with clear interfaces and responsibilities
Analyze and manage module dependencies to minimize coupling
Implement effective package organization strategies for maintainability
Apply complexity management techniques to large software systems

sections.title: Introduction to Software Architecture
learningGoals: Distinguish between architecture and detailed design
Understand the role of architecture in large-scale systems
Recognize architectural decisions and their long-term impact

subsections.title: What is Software Architecture?
keyPoints: Architecture as the fundamental organization of a system
High-level structure: components, relationships, and principles
Architecture vs. design: strategic vs. tactical decisions
Architectural decisions are costly to change later
Architecture addresses non-functional requirements (scalability, maintainability, performance)
examples: Building architecture analogy: floor plans vs. electrical wiring details
E-commerce system: presentation, business logic, data layers vs. individual class design
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Pyramid showing architecture at top (strategic, long-term), design in middle (tactical), and implementation at bottom (detailed)

subsections.title: Architectural Thinking
keyPoints: Focus on system-wide concerns rather than local optimization
Balancing competing quality attributes (performance vs. maintainability)
Thinking in terms of components and their interactions
Considering evolution and change over time
Stakeholder concerns: developers, operators, business owners
examples: Choosing microservices vs. monolith based on team structure and deployment needs
Trading database normalization for query performance in read-heavy systems
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Mind map showing architectural concerns: performance, scalability, maintainability, security, cost, team structure

exercises: Identify three architectural decisions in a system you've worked on and their consequences
List stakeholder concerns for a university course management system

sections.title: Layered Architectures
learningGoals: Understand the principles and benefits of layered architecture
Apply layering to separate concerns in large systems
Recognize common layering patterns and anti-patterns

subsections.title: Layering Principles
keyPoints: Separation of concerns through horizontal layers
Each layer depends only on layers below (strict layering)
Layers provide abstraction and hide implementation details
Common layers: presentation, application/business logic, data access, infrastructure
Benefits: maintainability, testability, team organization, technology independence
examples: Three-tier web application: UI layer, business logic layer, database layer
Operating system: application layer, system call interface, kernel, hardware abstraction
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Classic layered architecture diagram showing presentation → business logic → data access → database, with dependency arrows pointing downward

subsections.title: Implementing Layered Systems
keyPoints: Strict vs. relaxed layering (skipping layers)
Layer interfaces and contracts
Avoiding layer leakage (exposing lower-layer details)
Performance considerations: layer overhead
Package/namespace organization reflecting layers
examples: Good: Business layer returns domain objects; Bad: Business layer returns SQL ResultSet
Repository pattern isolating data access from business logic
MVC pattern as a layered architecture variant
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Code example showing proper layer separation with interfaces, contrasted with layer violation example

exercises: Design a layered architecture for an online banking system, identifying at least 4 layers
Identify layer violations in provided code snippets

sections.title: Component-Based Design
learningGoals: Understand components as architectural building blocks
Design components with clear interfaces and responsibilities
Apply component composition to build complex systems

subsections.title: Component Fundamentals
keyPoints: Components as independently deployable units with well-defined interfaces
Encapsulation: hiding internal implementation
Contracts: required and provided interfaces
Component granularity: finding the right size
Component vs. module vs. class: different levels of abstraction
examples: Payment processing component with interfaces for different payment methods
Logging component used across multiple applications
UI components in modern frameworks (React, Angular)
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Component diagram showing a component with provided interfaces (lollipop notation) and required interfaces (socket notation)

subsections.title: Component Design Principles
keyPoints: Single Responsibility Principle at component level
High cohesion within components
Low coupling between components
Interface segregation: multiple specific interfaces over one general interface
Dependency inversion: depend on abstractions, not concretions
examples: Email notification component separated from SMS notification component
Authentication component with separate interfaces for different authentication methods
Plugin architecture allowing component replacement
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Before/after comparison showing tightly coupled components refactored to use interfaces

exercises: Identify components and their interfaces for a hotel reservation system
Refactor a monolithic system diagram into well-defined components

sections.title: Module Dependencies and Coupling
learningGoals: Analyze dependency structures in large systems
Identify and resolve problematic dependencies
Apply principles to minimize coupling

subsections.title: Understanding Dependencies
keyPoints: Types of dependencies: compile-time, runtime, data dependencies
Dependency graphs and their analysis
Cyclic dependencies and their problems
Transitive dependencies and dependency chains
Measuring coupling: afferent and efferent coupling
examples: Module A uses classes from Module B (compile-time dependency)
Circular dependency between User and Order modules
Dependency explosion in poorly structured systems
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Dependency graph showing modules as nodes and dependencies as directed edges, highlighting a cycle

subsections.title: Managing and Reducing Coupling
keyPoints: Acyclic Dependencies Principle (ADP)
Stable Dependencies Principle (SDP): depend in direction of stability
Stable Abstractions Principle (SAP): stable packages should be abstract
Breaking cycles: dependency inversion, introducing interfaces, merging packages
The cost of coupling: ripple effects, testing difficulty, reuse barriers
examples: Breaking UI-Business Logic cycle by introducing events/observers
Using dependency injection to invert dependencies
Facade pattern reducing coupling to subsystems
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Dependency structure matrix (DSM) showing module dependencies, with cycle highlighted

exercises: Analyze a dependency graph and identify all cycles
Propose refactorings to break identified dependency cycles

sections.title: Package Organization Strategies
learningGoals: Apply effective package organization principles
Choose appropriate packaging strategies for different contexts
Understand the relationship between packages and architecture

subsections.title: Package Organization Approaches
keyPoints: Package by layer vs. package by feature vs. package by component
Package by layer: groups by technical role (controllers, services, repositories)
Package by feature: groups by business capability (user management, billing)
Package by component: groups by architectural component
Screaming architecture: structure reveals intent
examples: Package by layer: com.app.controllers, com.app.services, com.app.repositories
Package by feature: com.app.user, com.app.billing, com.app.inventory
Hexagonal architecture package structure with ports and adapters
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Side-by-side comparison of package-by-layer vs. package-by-feature directory structures

subsections.title: Package Principles and Best Practices
keyPoints: Common Closure Principle (CCP): classes that change together, package together
Common Reuse Principle (CRP): classes that are used together, package together
Release Reuse Equivalency Principle (REP): reuse granularity = release granularity
Package cohesion: keeping related things together
Package naming conventions and hierarchy
examples: Packaging all database migration utilities together (CCP)
Separating rarely-changed core from frequently-changed features
Maven/Gradle module structure reflecting architectural components
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Package diagram showing proper cohesion with related classes grouped together

exercises: Reorganize a given package structure from package-by-layer to package-by-feature
Evaluate package cohesion in a provided system and suggest improvements

sections.title: Managing Complexity in Large Systems
learningGoals: Recognize sources of complexity in software systems
Apply techniques to manage and reduce complexity
Design systems that remain maintainable as they grow

subsections.title: Sources and Types of Complexity
keyPoints: Essential complexity (problem domain) vs. accidental complexity (solution)
Complexity drivers: size, dependencies, state, concurrency, distribution
Cognitive load: how much developers must understand
Technical debt and its compounding effects
Measuring complexity: cyclomatic complexity, coupling metrics, lines of code
examples: Essential: tax calculation rules; Accidental: over-engineered framework
Spaghetti code with high cyclomatic complexity
Microservices adding distributed system complexity
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Graph showing complexity growth over time with and without active management

subsections.title: Complexity Management Techniques
keyPoints: Abstraction: hiding details behind simpler interfaces
Decomposition: breaking large problems into smaller ones
Modularity: independent, replaceable components
Information hiding: minimizing what modules expose
Separation of concerns: orthogonal responsibilities
Incremental development: managing complexity over time
examples: Database abstraction layer hiding SQL complexity
Microkernel architecture isolating core from plugins
Domain-Driven Design bounded contexts reducing cognitive load
Strangler Fig pattern for gradual legacy system replacement
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Complexity management strategy diagram showing abstraction layers, module boundaries, and information hiding

subsections.title: Architectural Patterns for Complexity
keyPoints: Pipes and Filters: decomposing data processing
Event-Driven Architecture: decoupling through events
Microservices: independent deployment and scaling
Monorepo vs. polyrepo: managing code organization
Conway's Law: architecture reflects organizational structure
examples: Unix pipes composing simple tools
Event sourcing separating write and read models
Netflix microservices architecture
Team structure aligned with bounded contexts
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Event-driven architecture diagram showing loosely coupled components communicating via event bus

exercises: Identify sources of accidental complexity in a provided system design
Propose an architectural refactoring to reduce complexity in a monolithic application
Design a complexity management strategy for a growing startup's codebase

sections.title: Conclusion and Practical Application
learningGoals: Synthesize architectural concepts into coherent design approach
Apply learned principles to real-world scenarios
Understand the relationship to design patterns and advanced topics

subsections.title: Architectural Decision Making
keyPoints: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs): documenting key decisions
Trade-off analysis: evaluating alternatives
Fitness functions: automated architectural governance
Evolutionary architecture: designing for change
Connection to design patterns (Observer, Visitor, etc.)
examples: ADR example: choosing REST over GraphQL for API
Trade-off matrix comparing monolith vs. microservices
Fitness function checking dependency rules in CI/CD
subsections.suggestedDiagram: ADR template showing structure: context, decision, consequences, status

subsections.title: Summary and Next Steps
keyPoints: Architecture as foundation for software construction
Key principles: separation of concerns, low coupling, high cohesion
Architectural styles as reusable solutions
Continuous architectural refinement
Preview: design patterns as micro-architectural solutions
Connection to Architectural Strategy course (2025-MCSSE-SE-03)
examples: Case study: refactoring a real system using learned principles
Architecture evolution timeline of a successful product
subsections.suggestedDiagram: Concept map connecting all lecture topics: layering, components, dependencies, packages, complexity management

exercises: Write an ADR for an architectural decision in your current or past project
Complete a comprehensive architectural design for a medium-scale system incorporating all learned principles
